headline: Zelensky says 76 Russian strikes on energy/oil/gas since Trump's 'energy weapon truce' declaration'
dek: Zelensky said Russia has conducted 76 targeted strikes against Ukraine's energy, oil and gas sectors since Trump's 'energy weapon truce' declaration (substations hit overnight in Vinnytsia, Zhytomyr, Khmelnytskyi, Odesa; tens of thousands lost power). He also claimed Starlink operations in Ukraine…
sources: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy (statements via Ukrinform/NV/Osna.fm); Ukraine Air Force overnight report (Iskander-M + 180 drones, 152 downed, hits at 20 locations; Zaporizhzhia woman 27 killed; Poltava 1 killed
fault_line: Did the energy-truce even last a day — and who gets to call a strike a violation?

sections.what_happened: Volodymyr Zelensky has accused Russia of conducting seventy-six targeted strikes against Ukraine's energy, oil and gas sectors since Donald Trump's 'energy weapon truce' declaration — with substations hit overnight in Vinnytsia, Zhytomyr, Khmelnytskyi and Odesa, leaving tens of thousands without power. He separately claimed that Starlink operations in Ukraine are restricted to speeds up to one hundred sixty-one kilometres per hour, making the system unusable on the interceptor drones designed to counter Russian attacks. Ukraine's Air Force reported an overnight barrage of Iskander-M missiles and one hundred eighty drones, with one hundred fifty-two downed and hits at twenty locations; a twenty-seven-year-old woman was killed in Zaporizhzhia, and one person was killed and two injured in Poltava.
sections.what_verified: The Air Force's overnight figures are corroborated across Ukrainian outlets — NV, Ukrinform, RBC-Ukraine — and the Anadolu Agency. The residential casualties in Zaporizhzhia and Poltava are corroborated across Ukrainian media. Russia's parallel claims — the defence ministry's one thousand fifteen drones destroyed, Moscow mayor Sobyanin's five hundred twelve drones toward the capital — are reported by Russian outlets. What is NOT verified: the seventy-six count is Zelensky's figure alone; the Starlink speed-restriction claim has no independent confirmation; and the 'energy weapon truce' declaration itself needs sourcing before anyone can judge whether it was violated.
sections.what_disputed: Both sides claim to be the victim of escalation on the same night. Zelensky says Russia violated the energy truce seventy-six times; Moscow says it destroyed over a thousand Ukrainian drones, implying Kyiv is the escalator. The Starlink claim — that a one-hundred-sixty-one-kilometre-per-hour cap cripples interceptor use — is technically specific and entirely single-sourced to Zelensky. No Russian confirmation of any truce, its terms, or its violation exists in the material reviewed.
sections.why_matters: If the energy-truce framework was real, seventy-six strikes would mean it lasted about a day — which tells you everything about where this war's diplomacy stands. The Starlink claim matters differently: it puts Elon Musk's constellation at the centre of Ukraine's air defence, and any degradation of it — by restriction, throttling or politics — directly translates into more missiles getting through. The heaviest night exchanges in weeks, on both sides' telling, suggest the escalation ladder is being climbed while the diplomats talk about truces.
sections.context: Energy infrastructure has been the war's winter battlefield for three years — each heating season brings a Russian campaign against the grid and a Ukrainian scramble to repair it. Trump's 'energy weapon truce' declaration, whatever its precise terms, was presented as a diplomatic achievement. Starlink has been Ukraine's indispensable communications and drone-guidance backbone since twenty twenty-two, and any constraint on it touches everything from frontline coordination to interceptor operations.

totw_analysis: Two accusations, one pattern: Zelensky is building a case, not just reporting a night. The seventy-six strikes claim needs the truce to have existed in a form anyone can check — and right now the truce itself is the least-sourced part of the story. That does not make the claim false; it makes it a primary-source accusation, and honest journalism labels it as such. The Western press will largely print the number as fact. We will not. The Starlink claim is the more interesting one, because it is falsifiable in a way the strike count is not: either the one-hundred-sixty-one-kilometre-per-hour restriction exists or it does not, and SpaceX could settle it in a sentence. That nobody has settled it tells you the claim is doing political work — reminding Washington, and Musk, that Ukraine's air defence runs on American private infrastructure, and that any friction in that pipeline has a body count. Read the Russian side of the ledger with the same scepticism: one thousand fifteen drones destroyed in a night is the kind of round number that survives no audit. Both capitals are describing the same sky and seeing different wars. The thing both accounts agree on — the heaviest exchanges in weeks, civilians dead in Zaporizhzhia and Poltava, tens of thousands without power — is the part that is verified. Start there, and treat everything else as what it is: two governments arguing over who escalated, while the grid burns.
